question: What exact firmware identity and AP address layout does the P65 3.100.043 image expose?
control_flow_evidence: The supplied IDA 9.4 loader accepted the extracted AP only after validating the entry stub, mapped Thumb pointer, footer base and FLASH_BASE/FLASH_NC_BASE/OTA_CODE_OFFSET aliases.
The decompiled XIP startup function _start begins at 0x0C0C0010; the mapped entry pointer at file offset 0x64 is 0x0C0C0015.
The exact AP contains ro.build.version=3.100.043 and ro.build.id=3.100.043 at XIP 0x0C3BF9EC, and the internal product ID miwear.watch.p65 at XIP 0x0C2A7B14.
The validated boot/build-info block begins at XIP 0x0CBFF30C and contains CHIP=best1502p, KERNEL=NUTTX, BUILD_DATE=Sep 12 2026 07:22:16 and REV_INFO=d516af0:nx_best1502p_ap.
unsafe_assumptions: The marketing model name is not established; P65 and miwear.watch.p65 are recorded as internal identifiers only.
The identity bytes are statically recovered but have not been checked on a physical P65 device.
The full OTA archive and AP payload are different artifacts; the target pack is bound to the exact vela_ap.bin payload SHA-256, while the archive SHA-256 is retained in provenance.
recommended_probe: After an exact-P65 bootstrap exists, run the generated identity guard on the device before exposing any firmware calls; keep all subsystem callables disabled until separately audited.
